name: Angle
definition: Denotes the angle at a vertex, named by three points with the vertex in the middle: ∠ABC has its vertex at B.

examples.explanation: The angle at B is a right angle.

name: Degree
definition: Measures angles with 360 degrees in a full turn. A right angle is 90°.

examples.explanation: A half turn in both units.

sources.label: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e

name: Radian
definition: Measures angles by arc length on the unit circle: a full turn is 2π radians. Calculus uses radians because derivative formulas for sine and cosine hold only in radians.

examples.explanation: Half a turn in radians and degrees.

name: Triangle
definition: Names a triangle by its three vertices. △ABC is the triangle with corners A, B and C.

examples.explanation: Two triangles with matching sides and angles.

name: Congruent
definition: States that two figures have exactly the same shape and size: one can be moved onto the other. Differs from similarity, which allows different sizes.

examples.explanation: Matching sides and matching angles.

name: Similar (geometry)
definition: States that two figures have the same shape but possibly different sizes: matching angles with proportional sides. The tilde has other uses (asymptotic, distributions) read from context.

examples.explanation: Same angles; one triangle is a scaled copy of the other.

contexts.meaning: X ~ N(0,1) means X follows that distribution.
f ~ g means their ratio tends to 1.

name: Parallel
definition: States that two lines never meet: they keep a constant distance and share a direction. Tick marks on diagrams show which lines are parallel.

examples.explanation: Lines l and m never intersect.

name: Perpendicular
definition: States that two lines meet at a right angle. In vector work the same sign means orthogonal: the inner product is zero.

examples.explanation: Lines l and m meet at 90 degrees.

name: Segment, ray and line notation
definition: A bar over two points names the segment joining them; an arrow names the ray starting at the first point through the second. A double-headed arrow names the whole line.

examples.explanation: The segment from A to B is 5 units long.

name: Arc notation
definition: Names the arc of a circle between two points. The minor arc is the shorter way round; naming three points disambiguates the major arc.

examples.explanation: The arc from A to B subtends 60 degrees.

name: Distance formula
definition: Gives the straight-line distance between two points from their coordinates. It applies Pythagoras to the horizontal and vertical separations.
reading: “d equals root of (x-two minus x-one squared plus y-two minus y-one squared)”.

examples.explanation: Points (1,2) and (4,6) form a 3-4-5 triangle.

name: Midpoint formula
definition: Gives the point halfway between two points by averaging each coordinate separately.

examples.explanation: Halfway from (0,0) to (4,6).

name: Slope
definition: Measures a line's steepness as rise over run: vertical change divided by horizontal change. Positive slopes climb; negative slopes fall; zero is flat; undefined means vertical.

examples.explanation: Up 4 for every 3 across.

name: Pi (circle constant)
definition: The ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter, about 3.14159. It is irrational: its decimals never repeat or terminate.

examples.explanation: Circumference from radius r.
Area from radius r.

name: Sine
definition: In a right triangle, the ratio of the side opposite an angle to the hypotenuse. Extended to all angles, it gives the y-coordinate on the unit circle.

examples.explanation: The opposite side is half the hypotenuse.

name: Cosine
definition: In a right triangle, the ratio of the side adjacent to an angle to the hypotenuse. On the unit circle it gives the x-coordinate.

examples.explanation: The adjacent side is half the hypotenuse.

name: Tangent
definition: In a right triangle, the ratio of the opposite side to the adjacent side; equivalently sine over cosine. It equals the slope of a line at that angle.

examples.explanation: Opposite equals adjacent at 45 degrees.

name: Reciprocal trigonometric functions
definition: The reciprocals of sine, cosine and tangent: cosecant is 1/sin, secant is 1/cos, cotangent is 1/tan. Secant here is a function, not a line cutting a curve.

examples.explanation: Secant is the reciprocal of cosine.

sources.label: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e
sources.license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (openstax.org footer); consulted as reference, original wording, no text reused

name: Inverse trigonometric functions
definition: Reverse sine, cosine and tangent: arcsin(y) is the angle whose sine is y. Results are restricted to a principal range so each input gives one angle.

examples.explanation: The angle with sine one half.

commonMistakes: Reading sin⁻¹ as 1/sin; the −1 denotes inversion, not a reciprocal.

name: Vector notation
definition: An arrow over a letter (or bold type) marks a quantity with direction as well as size. Vectors add tip-to-tail and scale by stretching.

examples.explanation: Three units across, four up; length 5.

name: Circle equation
definition: Describes a circle with center (h, k) and radius r: every point exactly r units from the center. It is the distance formula set equal to r.
reading: “the circle centered at h k with radius r”.

examples.explanation: Center (1, −2), radius 3.
